source.author: verg
source.text: Nec vero Alciden me sum laetatus euntem accepisse lacu, nec Thesea Pirithoumque, dis quamquam geniti atque invicti viribus essent.
source.text_original: Nec vero Alciden me sum laetatus euntem / accepisse lacu, nec Thesea Pirithoumque, / dis quamquam geniti atque invicti viribus essent.
source.text_english: Nor indeed did I rejoice to have received Alcides as I was going to the lake, nor Theseus and Pirithous, though they were born of gods and unconquered in strength.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nec vero Odrysius transtris impenditur Orpheus aut pontum remo subigit, sed carmine tonsas ire docet, summo passim ne gurgite pugnent.
reuse.text_original: nec vero Odrysius transtris impenditur Orpheus / aut pontum remo subigit, sed carmine tonsas / ire docet, summo passim ne gurgite pugnent.
reuse.text_english: Nor indeed is Orpheus, son of Odrysius, hung over benches, nor does he drive the sea with an oar; rather, with his song he teaches the shorn oars to go, so that everywhere they do not contend with the top of the wave.
